subject: Request: Review of June overage invoice and credit proposal
messages:
From: Emily Stone <finance@acme-corp.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rajiv Menon <cfo@acme-corp.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected overage on June invoice (invoice 2026-06-15)

Hi Laura,

We've just received invoice #2026-06-15 for $12,400 and it includes a one-time overage charge that we didn't anticipate. I've attached the invoice and our internal usage report for May–June for your review (invoice_20260615_acme.pdf, acme_usage_may-jun_2026.csv).

Can you explain how this charge was calculated and whether there's room for adjustment? We had an understanding that our committed capacity would cover the normal burst patterns through the renewal window. If there was a billing timing issue, we'd like to work with Redwood on an amendment or credit.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Stone
Director of Finance, Acme Corp
attachments: invoice_20260615_acme.pdf (pdf), acme_usage_may-jun_2026.csv (csv)

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Stone <finance@acme-corp.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on June invoice (invoice 2026-06-15)

Hi Emily — thanks for flagging this and for the attachments. I’m looping in Ben (sales) and Neha (CS) to get a quick read on whether this was a billing/window mismatch or an actual usage delta from the committed amount.

Quick ask: can you confirm which contract term the account was on for the May billing period (the renewal effective date was 2026-05-01 per our records)? That will help us map committed units to the invoiced window.

I'll aim to get a proposed resolution (amendment or one-time credit) back to you within 48 hours.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference | laura_bennett@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on June invoice (invoice 2026-06-15)

Laura — I pulled the raw billing logs. Short summary: there was a billing-window overlap between the committed capacity cutover (effective 2026-05-01) and an upstream meter that reported burst consumption for residual jobs spun up in the old region. Effectively, Acme consumed ~1.9M tokens beyond the committed unit bucket during the May 28–June 3 window that got billed in the June 15 invoice.

I'm attaching a draft credit calc (credit_calculation_draft.xlsx) that shows:
- Gross overage billed: $12,400
- Portion attributable to timing/billing-window artifact: $7,350
- Unexpected additional consumption (actual beyond committed, legitimate): $5,050

Given Acme's renewal last month and the fact the timing artifact is on us, I recommend we offer a one-time adjustment credit covering the $7.35k artifact and propose a goodwill discount of 10% on the remaining overage to help with churn risk. That would total ~ $8,885 in applied credit.

I'll leave final sign-off to you and finance (Marissa) for any accounting treatment.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on June invoice (invoice 2026-06-15)

Adding the CS lens — I reviewed usage patterns and can confirm the spike on May 30 correlates with a scheduled nightly batch that wasn't properly pinned to the dedicated pool. The jobs were routed to hosted capacity for a short period. We can prevent recurrence by adding a routing rule and pin for similar jobs.

From a customer-success perspective, we should:
- Offer the billing-window credit for the $7,350 timing error (on Redwood).
- Propose a 10% courtesy discount on the remaining $5,050 as Ben suggested (customer-facing goodwill).
- Follow up with a short runbook for Acme's infra team on pinning pools.

I'll draft the runbook and include it in the post-resolution packet if we have Ben/Laura sign-off on the credit.

—Neha
Neha Kapoor
Customer Success, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Stone <finance@acme-corp.com>, Rajiv Menon <cfo@acme-corp.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on June invoice (invoice 2026-06-15)

Hi Emily / Rajiv — thank you for your patience. Internal review indicates the invoice includes two components: the timing/billing-window artifact ($7,350) which is on us, and legitimate excess consumption ($5,050).

Proposed resolution:
- Redwood will apply a one-time invoice credit of $7,350 to fully cover the timing artifact.
- Redwood will apply a 10% courtesy discount to the remaining $5,050 overage (credit = $505).
- Net customer responsibility after credits: $12,400 - $7,350 - $505 = $4,545.

If that works for Acme, we'll issue a credit memo and an amended invoice within 5 business days. We will also provide a short technical runbook to prevent the routing issue in future. Attached is the internal credit_calculation_draft.xlsx for your review.

Please reply with approval and any preferred billing contacts for the credit memo.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
attachments: credit_calculation_draft.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Rajiv Menon <cfo@acme-corp.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Emily Stone <finance@acme-corp.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected overage on June invoice (invoice 2026-06-15)

Laura / team — thanks for the quick investigation and the clear breakdown. Acme accepts the proposed resolution (one-time credit of $7,350 plus the 10% courtesy reduction on the remaining overage). Please issue a formal credit note and an amended invoice showing net due $4,545 and send both to finance@acme-corp.com.

One ask on our side: please include a short line item on the credit note referencing this as a "billing-window timing correction" for our audit trail. Once we have the amended invoice we will process payment on the net balance.

Regards,
Rajiv Menon
CFO, Acme Corp
